extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and organizations invited to comment on an FTC petition for rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Notice announcing receipt of a petition for rulemaking by the Federal Trade Commission and soliciting public comments; describes how, when, and what commenters may submit and explains procedural limits on the petition's legal effect. Useful for anyone preparing or filing comments on this specific FTC docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline and docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must identify the petition docket number and be filed by January 2, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'Comments must identify the petition docket number and be filed by January 2, 2026.' Ensure your submission includes the docket number (FTC-2025-0792) and is timely filed by the stated close date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method and portal for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may view the petition and submit written comments concerning its merits by using the Federal eRulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments on Regulations.gov. The notice directs users to that portal and to 'Follow the online instructions for submitting comments.' Do not assume alternate submission routes unless the notice provides them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit sensitive personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should not include sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers; dates of birth; driver's license numbers or other state identification numbers; passport numbers; financial account numbers; or credit or debit card numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'In particular, your comment should not include any sensitive personal information, such as your or anyone else's Social Security number; date of birth; driver's license number or other state identification number, or foreign country equivalent; passport number; financial account number; or credit or debit card number.' Remove or redact such items before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit sensitive health information
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should not include sensitive health information, such as medical records or other individually identifiable health information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'You are also solely responsible for making sure your comment does not include any sensitive health information, such as medical records or other individually identifiable health information.' If health matters are relevant, summarize without individually identifiable details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit trade secrets or privileged commercial/financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should not include 'trade secret or any commercial or financial information which . . . is privileged or confidential' as provided by section 6(f) of the FTC Act and FTC Rule 4.10(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text cites statutory/regulatory authority: '—as provided by section 6(f) of the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. 46(f), and FTC Rule 4.10(a)(2).' If you believe information is privileged/confidential, follow the agency's procedures for asserting confidentiality rather than publicly filing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public nature of submissions / responsibility for content
rubrics_metrics.description: Because your comment will be placed on the publicly accessible website at Regulations.gov, you are solely responsible for ensuring it does not include sensitive or confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'Because your comment will be placed on the publicly accessible website ... you are solely responsible for making sure your comment does not include any sensitive or confidential information.' Treat all filings as potentially public unless you have followed procedures to request confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and responsiveness determine inclusion in public record
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to statutory/regulatory notice, the petition has been placed on the public record for 30 days and 'All timely and responsive comments submitted in connection with this petition will become part of the public record.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comments are both timely (filed by the deadline) and responsive to the petition's subject matter if you want them to be included in the administrative record for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review, redaction, and withholding of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.' Expect possible delays and redactions; do not rely on immediate public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may comment and the scope of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may submit comments in support of or in opposition to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'Any person may submit comments in support of or in opposition to the petition.' Comments may present arguments, evidence, or viewpoints relevant to whether the Commission should grant the petition to initiate rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission consideration timing and possible dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not consider the petition's merits until after the comment period closes. It may grant or deny the petition in whole or in part, and it may deem the petition insufficient to warrant commencement of a rulemaking proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'The Commission will not consider the petition's merits until after the comment period closes. It may grant or deny the petition in whole or in part, and it may deem the petition insufficient to warrant commencement of a rulemaking proceeding.' The notice's purpose is to gather public input to aid that determination; publication does not determine final outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication does not change legal status of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of this petition is pursuant to the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure and does not affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'Publication of this petition is pursuant to the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure and does not affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition.' Treat the notice as procedural for soliciting comment, not as a substantive agency decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find background documents and docket materials
rubrics_metrics.description: You may read background documents or comments received at https://www.regulations.gov at any time; the petition itself is available identified by docket number FTC-2025-0792.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Regulations.gov to access the petition (FT C-2025-0792), supporting documents, and any submitted comments for context when preparing your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and procedural information
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information is provided for the Office of the Secretary (phone: 202-326-2514, email: ElectronicFilings@ftc.gov) and the Commission notes the authority for the notice (15 U.S.C. 46; 15 U.S.C. 57a; 5 U.S.C. 601 note).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided contact details for procedural questions. Cite the docket number in inquiries. The authority citations indicate statutory bases for the notice and comment period.
